source_title: Entertainment Tiger Shroff Case: Zigana Pistol Bought For Rs 2.50 Lakh In Amritsar, Police Tracing Supplier
source_excerpt:
The investigation into the Tiger Shroff firing case has revealed crucial details about the purchase of weapons used in the attack. According to Mumbai Crime Branch sources, the Zigana pistol used in the firing was purchased in Amritsar for Rs 2.50 lakh. Along with the pistol, 20 rounds of ammunition were also procured. The police are now trying to identify the person who supplied the weapons and uncover the network involved.
According to sources, the accused arranged the pistol and ammunition from Amritsar on the instructions of Anil Pandit, a member of the Bishnoi gang. Rs 2.50 lakh was paid for the weapons. The investigation has revealed that the accused, Kunal, Sumit and Jatin, travelled directly to Amritsar with the money. There, they collected the pistol and ammunition from an undisclosed location.
According to sources familiar with the investigation, the accused left the money they had brought for the purchase at the same undisclosed location in Amritsar from where they collected the pistol and ammunition. However, the identity of the person who supplied the weapons and ammunition remains unknown. The Crime Branch is working to identify the individual to trace the entire network involved in the purchase and supply of the weapons.

Investigators are also trying to establish how the accused came into contact with the arms supplier and who else was involved in the deal. For now, identifying the person who supplied the weapons in Amritsar remains a key part of the investigation.

On October 18, shots were fired at Tiger Shroff’s car as he was returning home after playing football. Two men allegedly attacked his vehicle, while a third was waiting for them on a bike. Tiger was unharmed in the incident and escaped safely. Mumbai Police have arrested 11 accused in connection with the case so far, and police have invoked the stringent Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) against all of them.
